Case Management is the initial workspace inside an incident investigation where users establish the core case record, assemble the investigation team, and collect contextual and evidentiary sources. 

1. Key Workspace Elements

• Investigation Details: Houses structured factual data such as the event narrative, dates, harm and severity metrics, organization units, location parameters, external system references, and third-party contractors.

• People on the Investigation: Separates the Incident Created By user from human collaborators. Collaborators can be assigned roles (e.g., Commenter) to view, comment, or edit cases. 

• AI Investigation Team: Features an Investigation Lead (Haven Al) to 
orchestrate analysis alongside specialized supporting experts (e.g., 
Engineering, OSHA & Regulatory, Safety Programs, Equipment & PPE, 
Workplace Conditions, Training & Communication). 

• Auto-Collected Evidence and Context: Automatically pulls structured data 
from the Haven Industry and Knowledge Graphs, including:

• Regulatory: Industry standards and compliance exposure. 
• Company Programs: Relevant internal customer documentation. 
• Witness Statements: Collected via direct secure requests tracking status,
language, and deadlines.
• Weather Conditions: Retrieved automatically based on the incident date 
and location. 

2. Evidence Upload & Controls


• File Types & Limits: Accepts PDF, Word, PowerPoint, text, images, and 
videos. Size limits are 10 MB for general files and 50 MB for videos (Word and 
PowerPoint documents are automatically converted to PDF before 
processing).

• Evidence List Controls:
- Restricted: Flags sensitive evidence to manage role-based privacy.
- Reference Only: Designates files as available for background reference
without treating them as primary
analytical inputs for downstream AI generation.
- Actions: Supports direct file downloading, deletion (where permitted), and 
visibility previews.

The Incident Timeline workspace translates assembled case evidence into an ordered, chronological account of events, highlighting discrepancies for human evaluation. 

1. How Haven Builds the Timeline

• Haven synthesizes case data—such as reports, witness statements, work records, and 
media—to extract time-relevant facts, group related elements, order them chronologically, 
and flag contradictions.

• Core Support Rule ("Conflicts Before Conclusions"): A timeline conflict indicates that the 
evidence presents multiple versions of events. Support assists with navigation and controls, 
but never chooses which witness 
is correct, invents missing times, or makes investigative decisions for the customer.

2. Anatomy of a Timeline Event

• Each event card functions as a compact evidence claim containing:

• Date and Time: Displayed in incident-local time.
• Description: A synthesized account of the action or condition (treated as customer-owned 
text).
• Source(s): Direct links back to the foundational evidence documents. 
• Status Markers & Controls: Rail markers (check marks for standard events, amber for 
warnings/conflicts), expand/collapse chevrons, and a three-legged menu allowing 
authorized users to Move Up, Move Down, or Delete events.
• Manual Event Creation: Users can add missing events via the Generate Event dialog by 
supplying a defensible incident-local timestamp and a neutral, evidence-backed description.

Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
Platform Overview

The Root Cause Analysis phase becomes available after the Incident Timeline has been accepted. During this phase, the platform analyzes the uploaded evidence and the accepted timeline to generate one or both of the following:

• Five Whys Analysis
• Fishbone (6Ms) Analysis

The platform may also:

Display requests for additional information or clarification.
Assign a confidence level (High, Medium, or Low) to the suggested RCA.
Allow users to accept the suggested RCA or continue refining the information before proceeding.

Once the suggested RCA is accepted, the Corrective Action phase becomes available.

Corrective Action & Preventive Action (CAPA)
Platform Overview

After the Root Cause Analysis has been accepted, the platform generates suggested Corrective Actions (CA) and Preventive Actions (PA) based on the accepted RCA.

For each suggested CAPA, the platform provides:

• A recommended corrective and/or preventive action.
• An Effort vs. Impact graph to help evaluate the recommendation.
• A description explaining the recommendation.

Options to:
• Accept the suggested CAPA.
• Modify the suggested CAPA.
• Reject the suggestion.
• Create a new CAPA manually.
• Assignment of an owner.
• Target implementation date.

Once a CAPA has been accepted and finalized, the final reporting phase becomes available.

AI - Artificial Intelligence Technology that enables computers to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, such as analyzing incidents and generating insights.
LLM - Large Language Model An AI model trained on vast amounts of text that understands and generates human-like language. Used to assist users by answering questions and summarizing information.
RAG - Retrieval-Augmented Generation An AI approach that combines an LLM with retrieved customer-specific information (such as Knowledge Graph data) to generate more accurate and context-aware responses.
KG - Knowledge Graph A structured database that stores relationships between incidents, assets, people, sites, procedures, and other customer data to provide context for AI.
RCA - Root Cause Analysis A process used to identify the underlying cause of an incident instead of only addressing its symptoms.
5 Whys - Five Whys An RCA method that repeatedly asks "Why?" to drill down to the root cause of a problem.
6Ms - Six Ms A Fishbone Diagram categorization method consisting of Man (People), Machine, Method, Material, Measurement, and Mother Nature (Environment) to help identify possible causes.
OCR - Optical Character Recognition Technology that converts text from scanned documents or images into editable digital text.
PDF - Portable Document Format A file format commonly used for sharing documents while preserving formatting.
UI - User Interface The screens, buttons, menus, and other visual elements users interact with in Haven.
UTC - Coordinated Universal Time The international standard time reference used to synchronize timestamps across different time zones.
ID - Identifier A unique value assigned to records such as incidents, users, or cases for easy identification.
API - Application Programming Interface A set of rules that allows Haven to communicate and exchange data with other software systems.
CSV - Comma-Separated Values A file format commonly used to import or export tabular data.

HavenSIGHT - Haven's AI-powered investigation platform that helps organizations manage incidents, investigations, evidence, and root cause analysis.

HavenEDGE - Haven's edge application that connects operational systems and devices to Haven by collecting and synchronizing data.

Case Management - The module used to organize an investigation by managing evidence, tasks, collaborators, witness requests, and corrective actions.

Incident Timeline - A chronological view of events related to an incident, helping investigators understand what happened and when.

Corrective Actions - Tasks created to prevent the same incident from happening again after the investigation identifies the root cause.

Auto Collected Evidence - Information automatically gathered by Haven from connected systems and data sources to support investigations.

Collaborator - A user invited to participate in an investigation by reviewing evidence or completing assigned tasks.

AI Expert - Haven's AI assistant that analyzes available information and provides recommendations or insights during investigations.

Witness Request - A request sent to witnesses to collect statements or additional information about an incident.

Confidence Level - Indicates how confident the AI is in its generated analysis (High, Medium, or Low). It reflects confidence in the AI's output, not whether the conclusion is definitely correct.

Five Whys - Identifies the root cause by repeatedly asking "Why?" until the underlying cause is found.
Fishbone Diagram (Ishikawa Diagram) - Organizes possible causes into categories (6Ms) to systematically investigate contributing factors.
Timeline Analysis - Uses the sequence of events to identify where failures or contributing factors occurred during an incident.

Customer Concern

Why does my Root Cause Analysis show Medium Confidence?

Agent Knowledge

Confidence is based on the amount, quality, and consistency of the information provided during the investigation.

A confidence rating does not necessarily mean the RCA is incorrect.

Sample Email Reply

Hi [Customer Name],

Thank you for contacting Haven Helpdesk.

The confidence indicator reflects how much supporting information is available for the generated Root Cause Analysis.

A Medium Confidence rating generally means there may be limited, incomplete, or inconsistent information available for the platform to analyze. It does not automatically mean the suggested Root Cause Analysis is incorrect.

You may review the available information, provide additional details if appropriate, or continue with the suggested analysis based on your organization's investigation process.

Please let us know if this answers your question or if you need further assistance.

Customer Concern

What do the confidence levels mean?

Sample Email Reply

Hi [Customer Name],

Thank you for contacting Haven Helpdesk.

The confidence level indicates how strongly the available information supports the suggested Root Cause Analysis.

• High Confidence – The available evidence consistently supports the suggested root cause.
• Medium Confidence – The available information generally supports the suggestion, but additional clarification may improve accuracy.

These confidence levels are intended to help guide your review and should not be considered a final determination. The investigation team should review the suggested analysis before accepting it.

Level 1 Support Playbooks & Triage

Common Case Management & Timeline Issues

• Customer Statement / Symptom:

- "My evidence is missing."
- "The AI ignored a document."
- "The timeline is wrong."
- "The event time is wrong."
- "I cannot add/edit/delete an event."
- "The conflict will not clear."

• Primary Support Checks

- Verify correct incident, file count, collapsed sections, upload success, Reference Only 
status, 
restrictions, and browser refresh.
- Check if the file was set to Reference Only, verify processing completion, upload timing 
relative to analysis generation, and text readability.
- Capture exact event details, displayed vs. expected wording/time, source documents, active 
conflicts, and timeline state.
- Check incident-local time zones, AM/PM selections, source timestamps, and conflict logs.
- Verify user role, incident ownership, workflow stage, Accepted state status, and required 
fields.
- Inspect source disagreements, saved event updates, the Resolve flow sequence, and 
browser state.

Level 1 Action & Escalation Thresholds

- Escalate when: The file is verified as fully uploaded and processed, yet persistently fails to 
appear.
- Escalate when: A valid, non-restricted file processed before generation is consistently 
omitted across tests.
- Escalate when: Processed evidence is consistently misrepresented after user review and 
corrections.
- Escalate when: Saved values continuously revert or display incorrectly relative to stored 
values.
- Escalate when: An authorized user meeting all prerequisites experiences persistent failures 
or errors.
- Escalate when: Completing the standard resolution workflow fails to update the conflict 
status.

High-Consequence Escalation Protocols

Immediate Escalation Triggers

Instantly escalate issues involving:
• Potential unauthorized evidence access or data exposure.
• Deletion or corruption of critical investigation records.
• Regulatory, legal, or formal compliance content.
• Any incident involving a fatality, serious injury, or SIF/PSIF case.

Complete Diagnostic Escalation Packet

When escalation is necessary, avoid sending full, unredacted screenshots. Provide a secure diagnostic packet containing:

• Customer name and environment (production vs. training).
• Incident title and identifier.
• Current workflow stage and timeline state.
• Affected user, role, and relationship to the incident.
• Specific event date, time, description, and sequence position.
• Conflict title, labels, summaries, and locations (inline vs. side panel).
• Exact source file names along with their Restricted or Reference Only flags.
• Expected behavior versus actual behavior, along with exact steps taken.
• Browser, version, session refresh steps, and whether the issue reproduces for other users.
• Protected screenshots omitting unnecessary personal, medical, or confidential data.

Introduction to Haven Safety AI

• Overview

Haven Safety AI is an AI-native safety intelligence platform designed to help organizations investigate workplace incidents, identify root causes, manage corrective actions, and strengthen organizational learning. It supports safety 
professionals by accelerating investigation activities while ensuring that final decisions remain under human control. The platform is intended to improve consistency, traceability, and defensibility throughout the incident investigation 
process.

• Core Principle

Every employee supporting or using Haven should understand the platform's primary operating principle:

• AI proposes. Humans decide.

All AI-generated summaries, timelines, root cause analyses, recommendations, and corrective actions are considered draft working material until they have been reviewed and approved by authorized personnel. Haven does not 
automatically finalize investigations, assign blame, or approve corrective actions.
Why Haven Exists

Organizations frequently encounter challenges during incident investigations, including:

- Information distributed across multiple systems and documents
- Variability in investigation quality
- Weak organizational learning
- Corrective actions that focus on task completion rather than risk reduction
- Loss of institutional knowledge as personnel change

Haven addresses these challenges by organizing evidence, supporting structured investigation workflows, and assisting investigators in producing more consistent and evidence-based findings.

• What Haven Is

Haven is designed to function as:

- An AI-native safety intelligence platform
- An investigation support system
- A structured workflow for incident investigations
- A collaborative workspace for investigators
- A decision-support platform grounded in evidence

Haven assists investigators by:

- Organizing evidence
- Drafting summaries
- Building incident timelines
- Suggesting possible root causes
- Recommending corrective actions
- Identifying patterns across investigations

Final responsibility always remains with the investigation team.

• What Haven Is Not

Employees should avoid describing Haven as:

- A replacement for safety professionals
- A replacement for existing EHS systems
- An autonomous investigation platform
- A system that automatically determines root causes
- A system that independently closes investigations

Instead, Haven should always be described as an AI-assisted decision-support platform.

• Platform Components

Although these names may not appear directly in the application's navigation, Haven is conceptually divided into two primary functional areas.

HavenSIGHT

Provides organization-wide visibility through:

- Dashboards
- Incident metrics
- Trends
- Reporting
- Incident lists
- Monitoring views

• HavenEDGE

Provides the investigation workspace where users perform:

- Case Management
- Evidence management
- Incident Timeline creation
- Root Cause Analysis
- Corrective Action management
- Report generation

A future platform component, havenIMPACT, is planned to deliver predictive analytics, leading indicators, and cross-incident trend analysis.

• Human Responsibilities

Employees using Haven are expected to:

- Review every AI-generated output
- Verify supporting evidence before approval
- Correct inaccurate or incomplete AI suggestions
-Make all final investigation decisions
- Ensure corrective actions are appropriate and complete
- Maintain accountability for the official investigation record

AI-generated content should never be accepted solely because it appears well written or confident. Supporting evidence must always be reviewed before approval.

Key Takeaways

- Haven is an AI-assisted safety investigation platform.
- AI accelerates investigations but never replaces professional judgment.
- All AI outputs are drafts until reviewed and approved.
- Human investigators remain accountable for every investigation outcome.
- Evidence validation is mandatory before accepting AI recommendations.

Regeneration Scenarios & Practice

Goal: Understand how Haven's regeneration system works, what triggers regeneration, how changes cascade through the investigation workflow, and how to guide users in safely regenerating and accepting updated analyses while preserving existing work.
Key Topics:
Regeneration Fundamentals: Haven detects upstream changes (evidence, timeline, or RCA) and flags downstream stages that require regeneration. Users control when regeneration occurs, and accepted work is never automatically overwritten.
Regeneration Triggers: Learn the events that trigger regeneration, including adding, deleting, or editing evidence files, resolving Timeline conflicts, editing or adding RCA causes, and re-accepting regenerated RCA analyses.
Scenario A – New Evidence Uploaded: Practice uploading new evidence after a Timeline and RCA have been accepted, regenerating the Timeline, reviewing updates, re-accepting it, and then regenerating the affected RCA.
Scenario B – RCA Changes: Learn how editing or manually adding a cause in Fishbone RCA automatically triggers regeneration for Corrective Actions, ensuring recommendations reflect the latest root causes.
Scenario C – Evidence Deletion Cascade: Understand the complete regeneration flow when evidence is deleted: Evidence → Timeline → RCA → Corrective Actions, with each stage regenerated and accepted in sequence.
Scenario D – RCA Cause Deletion: Practice deleting a Fishbone cause, re-accepting the RCA, and regenerating Corrective Actions to reflect updated recommendations without losing previously accepted work.
Support Best Practices: Reinforce the key helpdesk message that regeneration is expected behavior, not an error. Guide users to regenerate stages in order, review the results, and reassure them that accepted work is preserved until they choose to regenerate.

studio expertise).
- Core Value & Positioning: An AI-native safety intelligence platform designed as a copilot to help 
safety teams capture evidence, structure investigations, and uncover systemic risk.
- Responsible AI Rule: Al proposes, humans decide.
- Key Team Contacts: Joe Hanna (CEO - Mission & Escalations), Jim Wang (CTO - Tech &
Reliability), and Jaskiran Kaur (Program Manager - Logistics & Action Items).

Safety Fundamentals and Customer Language

• Goal: Master workplace safety vocabulary, the incident lifecycle, and industry frameworks to support 
customers in context

• Key Topics:
- Incident Lifecycle: Closed loop of 6 stages—Event occurs, Report/Notify, Preserve Evidence, 
Investigate/Analyze, Corrective/Preventive Actions, and Verify/Learn.
- Severity Ladder: Distinguishing between Near Misses, First Aid Cases, OSHA Recordables, Lost 
Time Injuries (LTI), and Serious Injuries or Fatalities (SIF).
- Causal Analysis: Differentiating Immediate (Proximate) Causes from Root Causes (systemic 
flaws).
- Hierarchy of Controls: Ranking control strength from top to bottom: Elimination, Substitution, 
Engineering Controls, Administrative Controls, and PPE.
- Industry Vocabularies: Hazard terminology across Utilities (e.g., Arc flash, LOTO), Construction 
(e.g., Focus Four, Trenching), and Oil & Gas (e.g., Process Safety Events, DROPS, Hot Work).

Incident Investigations and RCA Fundamentals

• Goal: Understand the mechanics of safety investigations and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) methods without becoming an investigator.

• Key Topics:
- Investigation Mindset: Prioritizing prevention over blame and evidence over assumptions. 
- Evidence Collection: Evaluating narratives, photos, video/audio, system logs, and witness 
statements.

• RCA Methodologies:
- Five Whys: Tracing linear chains to system conditions.
- Multi-Threaded Five Whys: Managing parallel causal pathways (e.g., equipment, people, 
environment, management systems).
- Fishbone Analysis: Categorizing factors across People, Process, Equipment, Environment, 
Materials, and Management.

• CAPA Linkage:
- Tying corrective/preventive actions directly back to root causes and scoring them on impact, effort, 
and confidence.

Case Management

• Goal: Learn how to manage incidents and organize investigation evidence.
• Key Topics:
- Creating and managing cases.
- Evidence management.
- Investigation workspace.
- Collaboration features.

Roles

• Goal: Understand user permissions and responsibilities within Haven.

• Key Topics:
- User roles.
- Permissions.
- Access control.
- Team responsibilities.

Auto Collected Evidence & Context

• Goal: Learn how Haven automatically gathers supporting information for investigations.

• Key Topics:
- Regulatory data.
- Weather information.
- Company programs.
- Witness statements.

Incident Timeline

• Goal: Build and review a chronological sequence of investigation events.

• Key Topics:
- Timeline generation.
- Evidence ordering.
- Event relationships.
- Investigation review.

Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
• Goal: Identify the underlying causes of incidents using Haven's RCA tools.

• Key Topics:
- RCA concepts.
- Analysis methods.
- Contributing factors.
- Findings.

Practical Lab – End-to-End Investigation

• Goal: Apply the complete Haven investigation workflow by creating and investigating a real incident from start to finish using the live platform.

• Key Topics:
- Create a new incident by entering incident details, location, and reviewing the submission before creating the case.
- Upload multiple evidence files, verify document types, and understand Haven's automatic document processing (OCR and PDF conversion).
- Retrieve regulatory information and historical weather data using Auto Collected Evidence & Context.
- Add and manage witness statements using the available invitation methods (Magic Link, Voice Call, or SMS).
- Complete the investigation by building the timeline, performing Root Cause Analysis (RCA), reviewing findings, and validating the end-to-end investigation workflow.

Helpdesk Operational Process Guide

• Goal: Understand the Haven × Santos helpdesk operating model, including core support processes, SLA expectations, escalation paths, and performance metrics to consistently deliver high-quality customer support.

Key Topics:
- Core Support Processes: Learn the end-to-end responsibilities of the helpdesk, including Issue Response, Application Support, Escalation Management, Knowledge Management, SLA Monitoring, and Change & Release Communication. Understand each 
process's purpose, triggers, expected actions, and ownership.
- Issue Response & Escalation: Handle critical incidents by acknowledging issues within SLA, creating high-priority tickets, notifying stakeholders, and escalating unresolved problems through Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 support (Jaskiran/Joe) when 
necessary.
- Application Support & Knowledge Management: Support users with application navigation, permissions, troubleshooting, and leverage the Knowledge Base to resolve issues efficiently. Document new solutions and recurring issues to continuously improve 
support resources.
- SLA Management: Understand ticket priority levels (P1–P4), response time targets, escalation paths, notification requirements, and review cadence to ensure incidents are handled according to service commitments.
- Performance Metrics & KPIs: Monitor operational success through key metrics including Tickets Closed, SLA Compliance Rate, Backlog Count, First Contact Resolution (FCR), Reopened Ticket Rate, Escalation Rate, Customer Satisfaction (CSAT), and 
Knowledge Base Usage.
- Continuous Improvement Mindset: Use ticket reports, SLA monitoring, customer feedback, and Knowledge Base updates to improve resolution speed, maintain service quality, and enhance the overall support experience.

Regeneration Scenarios & Practice

• Goal: Understand how Haven's regeneration system works, what triggers regeneration, how changes cascade through the investigation workflow, and how to guide users in safely regenerating and accepting updated analyses while preserving existing work.

• Key Topics:
- Regeneration Fundamentals: Haven detects upstream changes (evidence, timeline, or RCA) and flags downstream stages that require regeneration. Users control when regeneration occurs, and accepted work is never automatically overwritten.
- Regeneration Triggers: Learn the events that trigger regeneration, including adding, deleting, or editing evidence files, resolving Timeline conflicts, editing or adding RCA causes, and re-accepting regenerated RCA analyses.
- Scenario A – New Evidence Uploaded: Practice uploading new evidence after a Timeline and RCA have been accepted, regenerating the Timeline, reviewing updates, re-accepting it, and then regenerating the affected RCA.
- Scenario B – RCA Changes: Learn how editing or manually adding a cause in Fishbone RCA automatically triggers regeneration for Corrective Actions, ensuring recommendations reflect the latest root causes.
- Scenario C – Evidence Deletion Cascade: Understand the complete regeneration flow when evidence is deleted: Evidence → Timeline → RCA → Corrective Actions, with each stage regenerated and accepted in sequence.
- Scenario D – RCA Cause Deletion: Practice deleting a Fishbone cause, re-accepting the RCA, and regenerating Corrective Actions to reflect updated recommendations without losing previously accepted work.
- Support Best Practices: Reinforce the key helpdesk message that regeneration is expected behavior, not an error. Guide users to regenerate stages in order, review the results, and reassure them that accepted work is preserved until they choose to 
regenerate.

The account is newly created and no access scope has been assigned yet.
The user's SSO account has not yet been mapped to the correct Haven profile.

Process

Since this is your first time logging in, please contact your organization's Haven Administrator to verify that your account has been assigned the appropriate role and access scope. If your administrator confirms that everything has been configured correctly and you're still unable to view any data, please let us know, and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Topic:
A whole BU / division is
missing for me.
Content:
Possible Cause: 
The user's access scope does not include the Business Unit (BU) or division they are trying to access. 

Process: 
1. Confirm which Business Units or divisions the user can currently see. 
2. Verify which BU or division they believe is missing. 
3. Advise the user to contact their organization's Haven Administrator to request the necessary access update. 
4. If the administrator confirms the correct access has already been assigned and the issue persists, gather the details and escalate to the Haven Team if appropriate. 

Notes: 
*Access to Business Units and divisions is managed by the customer's Haven Administrator. 
*Level 1 Support does not grant or modify user access. 
*Ensure the user specifies the missing BU or division before directing them to their administrator. 

"Thank you for reaching out. Could you please let us know which Business Unit or division you're currently able to access, and which one you're expecting to see? 

If the missing BU or division hasn't been assigned to your account, you'll need to contact your organization's Haven Administrator, as they manage user access and permissions. If your administrator confirms the correct access has already been assigned and you're still unable to see it, please let us know and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Topic: My Colleague Sees an Incident I Can't
Content:
Process: 
Confirm which incident the user is unable to view. 
Ask whether another user can access the incident and, if so, what their role is (if known). 
Explain that incident visibility depends on each user's assigned role and access scope. 
If the customer confirms the user should have access to the incident, advise them to contact their organization's Haven Administrator to review and update the user's access. 

Notes: 
*Users may have different visibility based on their assigned role, Business Unit (BU), and division. 
*Level 1 Support does not modify user access or permissions. 
*If the administrator confirms the user has the correct access and the issue persists, gather the details and escalate to the Haven Team if necessary. 

'Thank you for reaching out. Incident visibility is based on each user's assigned role and access scope. If another user can view the incident but you cannot, it's possible that your account doesn't currently have access to the Business Unit or division where the incident resides. 

If you believe you should have access, please contact your organization's Haven Administrator to review your permissions. If they confirm your access is configured correctly and you're still unable to view the incident, please let us know and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Topic:
The BU/DIV filter doesn't
show the unit I need.
Content:
Possible Cause 
The filter only displays Business Units (BUs) and divisions that the user already has access to. 
A missing BU or division in the filter typically indicates an access scope issue, not a filter issue. 

Process: 
1. Confirm which BU or division the user is expecting to see in the filter. 
2. Explain that filters only display the BUs and divisions the user is authorized to access. 
3. Clarify the difference between: 
Filter – A temporary, user-selected view of accessible data. 
Access Scope – Permissions assigned by the organization's Haven Administrator. 
4. If the user should have access to the missing BU or division, advise them to contact their organization's Haven Administrator to review and update their access. 

Notes: 
*A missing BU or division in the filter is not typically a product bug. 
*Level 1 Support does not modify user access or permissions. 
*If the administrator confirms the user's access is correct and the BU/division is still missing from the filter, gather the details and escalate to the Haven Team if appropriate. 

"Thank you for reaching out. The BU/Division filter only displays the Business Units and divisions that your account has permission to access. If the unit you're looking for isn't listed, it may indicate that your current access scope doesn't include it. 

If you believe you should have access, please contact your organization's Haven Administrator to review your permissions. If they confirm your access is configured correctly and the issue persists, please let us know and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Possible Cause 
Dashboard totals and incident counts are based on each user's assigned access scope. 
Different users may see different totals if they have different roles or access permissions. 

Process: 
1. Confirm which dashboard, report, or list the users are comparing. 
2. Explain that totals are calculated based on the data each user is authorized to view. 
3. If the customer believes both users have identical roles and access scope, gather the following: 
Names or email addresses of both users 
Screenshots showing the differing totals 
The dashboard, report, or page where the discrepancy occurs 
4. If the customer confirms both users should have identical access, escalate the issue with the collected information. 

Notes: 
*Different totals are expected behavior when users have different access scopes. 
*Level 1 Support should only escalate after confirming (or if the customer insists) that both users have identical roles and permissions. 
*Include screenshots and both user accounts in the escalation to assist with the investigation. 

"Thank you for reaching out. Dashboard totals and incident counts are based on each user's assigned access scope, so it's expected for different users to see different totals if their permissions differ. 

If you believe both users have the same role and access, could you please provide the names or email addresses of both users along with screenshots of the differing totals? We'll be happy to investigate further.

Topic: Three layers decide what a user sees and does
Content:
Overview 

A user's visibility and permissions in Haven are determined by three layers: 

Filter (User-set, temporary) – Controls how data is displayed but does not change what the user has permission to view. 
Access Scope (Admin-set) – Determines which organizations, Business Units (BUs), and divisions the user can access. 
Role (Admin-set) – Determines what actions the user can perform (e.g., Manager vs. Investigator) and whether they can view only their own incidents or all incidents within their assigned scope. 

Process: 
1. Identify whether the issue is related to: 
A filter (display preference), 
An access scope (organization/BU/division visibility), or 
A role (permissions and actions). 
2. If the issue involves access scope or role, advise the user to contact their organization's Haven Administrator. 
3. Escalate only if the administrator confirms the configuration is correct and the issue persists. 

Notes; 
*Filters are temporary and controlled by the user. 
*Access scopes and roles are assigned by the customer's Haven Administrator. 
*Level 1 Support does not modify user roles or access scopes. 
*Requests to change roles or access should be routed to the customer's Haven Administrator. 

"Thank you for reaching out. User access in Haven is determined by three factors: your selected filters, your assigned access scope (Organization/BU/Division), and your user role. If your request involves changing your role or access scope, please contact your organization's Haven Administrator, as these permissions are managed by them. If your administrator confirms everything is configured correctly and the issue persists, please let us know and we'll be happy to investigate further.

Possible Cause: 
Excel (.xls / .xlsx) files are not a supported evidence upload format. 

Process: 
1. Confirm that the user is attempting to upload an Excel file. 
2. Explain that Excel files are not currently supported for evidence uploads. 
3. Ask the user to convert the Excel file to a supported format, such as: 
PDF (recommended) 
Text (if applicable) 
4. Have the user upload the converted file instead. 

Notes: 
Supported upload formats are PDF, Word, PowerPoint, text, image, and video. 
Word and PowerPoint files are automatically converted to PDF during processing. 
Excel files are not supported for evidence upload. 

"Thank you for reaching out. At this time, Excel (.xls / .xlsx) files aren't supported for evidence uploads in Haven. 

We recommend converting the spreadsheet to a PDF before uploading it. Once converted, please try uploading the PDF version. If you continue to experience issues with a supported file type, let us know and we'll be happy to investigate further.
